subject: Routing workshop sprint — availability, traffic splits & fallback tiering
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@boxdata.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@boxdata.io>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood for inference routing — hands-on sprint request

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Both engineering and infra here liked the model-tiering concept. We'd like to move from a demo to a short hands-on sprint: a focused 3-hour working session where we
- review a representative prompt set,
- agree on routing policies (region, tiering, fallbacks), and
- run a small load test to validate latency and KV cache behavior.

Can your team do a 90–180 minute block the week of May 25? Timezone: PDT (we're all in SF). Our preference is either Tue afternoon or Wed morning. We'll bring a 10–12 prompt sample and a traffic-split CSV.

Attached: poc-agenda-v1.pdf (draft) and example-traffic-split.csv.

Appreciate a quick options list so we can lock in the calendar.

— Alex
BoxData (Prospect)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@boxdata.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood for inference routing — hands-on sprint request

Alex —

Great to hear BoxData wants to move to a hands-on sprint. We can run a focused session that covers prompt review, routing policy decisions (region / tiering / fallbacks), and a short load sweep. Proposed slots (PT):

1) Tue 26 May, 13:30–16:00 PT (best for infra leads)
2) Wed 27 May, 09:00–11:30 PT (good for engineering + product)
3) Wed 27 May, 14:00–16:30 PT (backup, overlap for APAC folks if needed)

Prep requests:
- Please upload the 10–12 prompt examples and the CSV to the Drive link you sent.
- Indicate which prompts are latency-sensitive vs quality-sensitive (we'll propose model selections accordingly).
- If you have a preferred fallback order (e.g., smaller quantized model before a cross-region fallback), note that in a column in the CSV.

Aditya and Stephanie — looped in to advise on model tiering and for the load test run. If none of the slots work, send three alternate 1.5–3h blocks.

I'll hold the slots tentatively and send an invite once you pick one.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya@boxdata.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@boxdata.io>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood for inference routing — hands-on sprint request

Monica / Aditya —

Thanks — Tue the 26th 13:30–16:00 PT works best for our infra and security stakeholders. A couple of quick asks before the session:

- Can you confirm whether the short load sweep will simulate burst/batch patterns (we want to evaluate both steady-state + 30s bursts)?
- For the prompt review, we have a mix of user-facing prompts (high quality) and internal summarization prompts (latency critical). We'll tag them in the CSV as suggested.
- Security: will we need any pre-approved IP ranges or allowlists for the load generator?

If you can confirm the above, we'll finalize attendees.

Thanks — Priya (BoxData)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@boxdata.io>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@boxdata.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood for inference routing — hands-on sprint request

Priya / Alex —

Confirmed: Tue 26 May, 13:30–16:00 PT is locked. Calendar invite sent (link below). Quick answers to your asks:

- Load sweep: we'll run two phases during the session — (A) steady-state at your expected 75th percentile qps and (B) burst phase with 30s peak ramps at 3x baseline. We'll capture latency P50/P95/P99 and token cost estimates in real time.
- Prompt tagging: perfect — please include a column "sensitivity" with values quality|latency. We'll use that to pick the model tier per prompt.
- Security: For the short load sweep we'll provide a transient allowlist. Please share the IPs of your load generator and an approver email; our infra team will add them to the session window only.

Prep before the session (action items):
- BoxData: upload final CSV + prompt set to the Drive link and confirm time zone for any remote APAC observers.
- Redwood (Aditya): prepare 2 routing policy proposals: (1) latency-first (regional primary, local small-quant fallback), (2) cost-first (larger batching, cross-region fallback).
- Redwood (Stephanie): prepare a short demo script for KV caching behavior and per-token cost instrumentation.
- Redwood (Dylan): bring tracing hooks and a quick checklist for canary vs full rollout.

Attachments: I've reattached poc-agenda-v1.pdf for convenience and included example-traffic-split.csv.

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=mock-invite-123
Drive prep: https://drive.google.com/file/d/mock-doc-traffic-splits

See you on the 26th — thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
